title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed draft of the opening of EGA 0_IV, 'Différentielles et dérivations', §1 'Dérivations et extensions d'algèbres'. It is stray material in a folder about algebraic cycles. The neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on positivity cones P_i^+ and Lefschetz-type maps α_i, unrelated to this page; the faint mirror-image handwriting visible through the sheet suggests the paper was reused. The bottom-left number '38' is the draft's own pagination.

The opening NB says the differential notions will be developed using the 'formally simple' topological algebras of the 'Cohen' draft. 'Cohen' is evidently the draft that became EGA 0_IV §19 (formally smooth algebras, Cohen structure theorems). Only Def. 1.1 of that draft and some of the sorites in 1.2 will be used. A second NB says this text will absorb many results of Grothendieck's own draft 'Cohen différentiel', which will have to be recast.

Mathematics, in modern terms:
- Setup: A is a ring, B an A-algebra, and p: E → C a surjection of A-algebras whose kernel J satisfies J² = 0. Then J is a C-module, hence a B-module via u: B → C.
- Proposition 1.1: suppose v₁: B → E is an A-algebra map lifting u (the typescript says A → E, a typo). A map v₂: B → E is also an A-algebra lift of u if and only if D = v₂ − v₁ takes values in J and is an A-linear map satisfying the Leibniz rule D(fg) = f·Dg + (Df)·g.
- Remark: given the Leibniz rule, A-linearity is equivalent to D vanishing on the image of A → B (plus additivity, which is automatic here).
- Definition 1.2: derivations of a ring into a module, and A-derivations of B into a B-module J.
- Corollary 1.3: the set of A-algebra lifts of u through E is either empty or a principal homogeneous space (torsor) under Der_A(B, J).

This is the standard foundation for the infinitesimal lifting criterion, formal smoothness/étaleness, and the obstruction theory of square-zero extensions. It appears essentially verbatim as EGA 0_IV §20.1 (Publ. IHES 20, 1964). The draft therefore predates 1964, although the folder is dated 1965–c.1971.
errors: The typescript writes v₁: A → E; it must be v₁: B → E.
'Ait la même propriété' implicitly requires v₂ to be an A-algebra homomorphism, not just any lift of u as a map of sets.
1º ⇔ 1 bis needs D to be additive. This is automatic when D is a difference of ring homomorphisms, but not for an arbitrary map satisfying Leibniz.
The B-module structure on J (through u, using J² = 0 to make J a C-module) is used but not stated explicitly.

ideas.what: The lifts of an algebra homomorphism through a square-zero extension form either the empty set or a torsor under Der_A(B, J).
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of infinitesimal liftings / deformation theory of square-zero extensions

ideas.what: Developing differentials via 'formally simple' topological algebras from the 'Cohen' draft.
ideas.where_published: EGA 0_IV §19, where the published term is 'formellement lisse'

missed.claim: This is a historical drafting detail, not new mathematics. The working draft calls formally smooth algebras 'formellement simple' and refers to internal drafts titled 'Cohen' and 'Cohen différentiel', which were merged into EGA 0_IV §§19–20.
missed.quote: la notion d'algèbre topologique formellement simple, définie dans "Cohen"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents the genesis of EGA 0_IV and an abandoned terminology. This is of minor interest to historians of EGA only.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a routine, published EGA 0_IV §20 foundation. The only novelty is the draft terminology 'formellement simple' and the names of internal drafts, and the page is misfiled among the cycle-theory notes.
transcription_corrections: Arrows (→) are absent in the typescript and were supplied by the transcription. The typescript's own 'v₁: A → E' is a typo in the original, not in the transcription.
'contient' appears in the image as a struck/misspelled 'contimnt'.
The struck-out line before 'l'ensemble des relèvements' is an overtyped deletion and is correctly omitted.
The handwritten bottom-left '38' is the draft's pagination.
